cells.tense: What is owed and what is given move evenly between you and the people close to you, and you feel the level without measuring it.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Think of an arrangement between you and someone close that no longer fits. Let it finish, on your side, without a speech about why.
cells.core:
In the give and take close to you, you can feel when something has slipped out of proportion and put it back without keeping a tally. You give and receive in the same motion, and nobody owes anybody from last month. The people near you feel that evenness as much as you do.

What keeps it alive is endings. Pick an arrangement between you and someone close that once fit and doesn't now. Let it finish, from your side, with nothing said about why. What goes is the comfort of an old agreement you've kept going past its time. Waiting costs more than ending; the ending is cheaper now. Nobody needs to be told.
cells.sheetLine: You feel what's even and put it back without keeping score.
cells.verb: setting what has drifted out of proportion back to level

cells.tense: Between you and the people close to you, fairness will run as a ledger — who gave, who owes, what each side has earned.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: When you catch yourself tallying what someone close still owes you, carry it for an hour without ruling on it — no verdict, no reopening the books.
cells.core:
Close to the people who matter, fairness can start running as a running count. You know what was given, when, and what is still owed back, and the count runs whether or not you want it to. The check goes on the person who forgot your birthday. You are not wrong about what happened. The books have just started answering questions nobody asked.

The stronger move here is not a better count. Carry the next unsettled thing at the size it actually has — an hour of not deciding what it means about the person — and hold it there without tightening around it. That is harder than settling it. Anything you later say lands better for the wait.

cells.tense: What was owed to you went unclaimed, and asking for it never seemed like something you could do.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Pick a practice you do alone and do it again today, no audience. Repeat tomorrow if today works.
cells.core:
When fairness is running between you and the people close to you, you say what you are owed in plain words and it lands as ordinary — no drama. You can ask for a thing and hear no without it meaning anything about your worth. The ask is small and the answer does not shake you.

Here, what was owed to you went unclaimed, and the asking seemed like something you could not do. What you have instead is a practice kept quietly, alone, where nobody can watch it go wrong. Do it again today, the same plain version, even when it feels pointless. Asking gets easier on the strength of the doing, not the other way around.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking for what was yours. Start with the plain version, alone.

cells.tense: The tallying between you and the people close to you runs under the surface while you are not aware you are doing it.
cells.act: let a perception land without arguing it
cells.ask: Next time something a close one says pulls at you to even the score, let the first impression arrive and stay put, with no argument either way.
cells.core:
Between you and the people close to you, things get weighed and you are not aware of doing it. A comment lands, and a small account moves. If asked, you would say you were not keeping score. Others nearby could name the count.

You do not need to work out why the accounts are there. When something said pulls at you to even it, let the first impression arrive and stay put — one clean reading, no argument with it. The readings turn out accurate when nothing is done to them. Sitting with not knowing for a while is enough. The weighing goes on being seen without being added to.
